changedBeliefs: The `parameter-encoding-and-binding` open question — whether any blob-heavy parameter shape is dominated by encoding rather than SQLite stepping — is answered for the single-row blob write path. A `Uint8List` blob param is copied three times before it reaches a database page: (1) main->writer via the VM C++ serializer inside `SendPort.send`, (2) writer->native param arena in `allocateParams`, (3) arena->SQLite page in `sqlite3_step`. Copies (2) and (3) are irreducible; copy (1) is not. For 256 KB-512 KB blobs, copy (1) is a material fraction of the whole INSERT.

Wrapping large blob params in `TransferableTypedData` (a byte move, not a serializer deep copy) on the main->writer hop is a reproduced ~15-20% end-to-end win on 256 KB-512 KB single-row blob INSERTs: 256 KB -16.4%/-22.7%, 512 KB -10.4%/-11.8% across order-flipped passes, with every 256 KB/512 KB leg candidate-faster across ~7 passes. Sub-threshold controls (64 KB, 128 KB) flip sign across the order flip (exp 177 drift signature), confirming the wins clear the ~+-8-15% noise floor by reproducing same-direction. `TransferableTypedData.fromList` does a plain memcpy into external memory (cheap: 9 us for 256 KB vs a 316 us round-trip) and does NOT neuter its source, so the public contract holds.

The win is size-bounded, and the bounds are measured, not assumed. Transport microbenchmark: `TransferableTypedData` is -22.6% at 256 KB but +22.7% SLOWER at 64 KB (wrap overhead exceeds the saved serializer copy) and neutral at 4 MB (`fromList`'s own copy grows to ~144 us and the WAL write dominates). Hence the 256 KB threshold (matching the read-side `sacrificeByteThreshold`). This is the inverse of exp 005: that rejected a Dart binary codec for structured map *results* because encoding structure in Dart is slow; a raw blob *param* has no structure to encode, so a straight byte transfer beats the serializer.
nextSignals: The batch (`BatchRequest`) and coalesced-write (`MultiExecuteRequest`) paths still deep-copy blob params via the serializer — exp 234 deliberately scoped to single-row `ExecuteRequest`/`QueryRequest`. Open candidate: a blob-heavy `executeBatch` workload (e.g. N rows each carrying a >=256 KB blob) to test whether wrapping per-set blobs reproduces the same transfer fraction. Blocked on nothing but a bounded pass; the `blob_param_write_ab.dart` harness generalizes to batch.

The 256 KB threshold is a measured floor on an Apple M1 Pro / macOS box; the crossover between wrap-overhead and serializer-saving is machine-dependent. A production profile showing a different blob-size distribution (many 64-256 KB blobs, or predominantly multi-MB) would justify re-tuning `blobParamTransferThreshold` or gating it per-arch.

The main->writer serializer copy is now bypassed for large blobs, but the writer->arena copy (2) and arena->page copy (3) remain. Neither is reducible through the current Dart FFI surface (the arena must own stable native bytes for SQLITE_STATIC across the bind+step, and SQLite owns its pages), so future blob-param work should target transfer/scheduling, not copy elimination, unless a zero-copy Dart->native pin primitive ships.
